paragraphs.sourceText: The Pacific island nation of Palau has become home to the sixth largest marine world. The new marine reserve, now the largest in the Pacific, will--26-- no fishing or mining. Palau also established the world’s first shark sanctuary in 2009.

The tiny island nation has set aside 500,000 square kilometres-80 percent -of its maritime --27--, for full protection, That’s the highest percentage of an--28 --economic zone devoted to marine conservation by any country in the world. The remaining 20 percent of the Palau seas will be reserved for local fishing by individuals and small-scale-- 29-- fishing businesses with limited exports.

“Island --30--have been among the hardest hit by the threats facing the ocean,” said President. Tommy Remengesau Jr. in a statement. “Creating this sanctuary is a bold move that the people of Palau recognise as 31 to our survival. We want to lead the way in restoring the health of the ocean for future generation.”

Palau has only been an_ 32 nation for twenty years and has a strong history of environmental protection. It is home to one of the world’s finest marine ecosystems, with more than 1,300 species of fish and 700 species of coral.

Senator Hokkons Baules, lead 33 of the Palau National Marine Sanctuary Act, said the sanctuary will “help build a 34 future for the Palauan people by honoring the conservation traditions of our past”. These include the centuries-old custom of “bul”, where leaders would call a temporary stop to fishing for key species in order to give fish 35 an opportunity to replenish(补充).

paragraphs.sourceText: Data sharing: An open mind on open date
paragraphs.translationZh: 数据共享：对开放日期持开放态度

paragraphs.sourceText: A. It is a movement building steady momentum: a call to make research data, software code and experimental methods publicly available and transparent. A spirit of openness is gaining acceptance in the science community, and is the only way, say advocates, to address a 'crisis' in science whereby too few findings are successfully reproduced. Furthermore, they say, it is the best way for researchers to gather the range of observations that are necessary to speed up discoveries or to identify large-scale trends.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：这是一场正在形成稳定势头的运动：呼吁公开和透明地提供研究数据、软件代码和实验方法。开放精神正在获得科学界的认可，倡导者们表示，这是解决科学“危机”的唯一途径，因为成功重现的发现太少。此外，他们表示，这是研究人员收集加速发现或识别大规模趋势所需的观察范围的最佳方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. The open-data shift poses a confusing problem for junior researchers. On the one hand, the drive to share is gathering official steam. Since 2013, global scientific bodies have begun to back politics that support increased public access to research. On the other hand, scientists disagree about how much and when they should share date, and they debate whether sharing it is more likely to accelerate science and make it more robust, or to introduce vulnerabilities and problems. As more journals and funders adopt data-sharing requirements, and as a growing number of enthusiasts call for more openness, junior researchers must find their place between adopters and those who continue to hold out, even as they strive to launch their own careers.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 开放数据的转变给初级研究人员带来了一个令人困惑的问题。一方面，分享的动力正在积聚官方力量。自 2013 年以来，全球科学机构开始支持政治，支持增加公众参与研究的机会。另一方面，科学家们对于应该分享多少数据以及何时分享数据存在分歧，他们还争论分享数据是否更有可能加速科学发展并使其更加稳健，或者是否会引入漏洞和问题。随着越来越多的期刊和资助者采用数据共享要求，以及越来越多的爱好者呼吁更加开放，初级研究人员必须在采用者和继续坚持的人之间找到自己的位置，即使他们努力开创自己的职业生涯。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. One key challenge facing young scientists is how to be open without becoming scientifically vulnerable. They must determine the risk of jeopardizing a job offer or a collaboration proposal from those who are wary of-or unfamiliar with -open science. And they must learn how to capitalize on the movement's benefits, such as opportunities for more citations and a way to build a reputation without the need for conventional metrics, such as publication in high-impact journals.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 年轻科学家面临的一个关键挑战是如何保持开放而不在科学上变得脆弱。他们必须确定那些对开放科学持谨慎态度或不熟悉的人的工作机会或合作提案受到损害的风险。他们必须学会如何利用该运动的好处，例如获得更多引用的机会以及无需传统衡量标准（例如在高影响力期刊上发表文章）即可建立声誉的方法。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Some fields have embraced open data more than others. Researchers in psychology, a field rocked by findings of irreproducibility in the past few years, have been especially vocal sup-porters of the drive for more-open science. A few psychology journals have created incentives to increase interest in reproducible science — for example, by affixing an ‘open-data’ badge to articles that clearly state where data are available. According to social psychologist Brian Nosek, executive director of the Center for Open Science, the average data-sharing rate for the journal Psychological Science, which uses the badges, increased tenfold to 38% from 2013 to 2015.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 有些领域比其他领域更接受开放数据。心理学领域的研究人员在过去几年中因不可重复性的发现而震动，尤其是推动更加开放的科学的坚定支持者。一些心理学期刊制定了激励措施，以提高人们对可重复科学的兴趣，例如，在明确说明数据可用的文章上贴上“开放数据”徽章。开放科学中心执行主任、社会心理学家布莱恩·诺塞克 (Brian Nosek) 表示，从 2013 年到 2015 年，使用这些徽章的《心理科学》杂志的平均数据共享率增加了十倍，达到 38%。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Funders, too, are increasingly adopting an open-data policy .Several strongly encourage, and some require, a date-management plan that makes data available .The US National Science Foundation is among these, Some philanthropic (慈善的) funders, including the Bill &Melinda Gates Foundation in Seattle, Washington, and the Wellcome Trust in London, also data mandate open data from their grant recipients.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 资助者也越来越多地采用开放数据政策。一些资助者强烈鼓励，有些要求制定数据管理计划，以提供数据。美国国家科学基金会就是其中之一。一些慈善资助者，包括华盛顿州西雅图的比尔和梅琳达·盖茨基金会以及伦敦的威康信托基金，也要求其资助者开放数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. But many young researchers, especially those who have not been mentored in open science, are uncertain about whether to share or to stay private. Graduate students and postdocs, who often are working on their lab head's grant, may have no choice if their supervisor or another senior opposes sharing.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 但许多年轻的研究人员，尤其是那些没有接受过开放科学指导的研究人员，不确定是否要分享或保持私密。经常靠实验室负责人资助工作的研究生和博士后，如果他们的导师或其他前辈反对分享，他们可能别无选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. Some fear that the potential impact of sharing is too high, especially at the early stages of a career." Everybody has a scary story about someone getting scooped(被抢先),” says New York University astronomer David Hogg. Those fears may be a factor in a lingering hesitation to share data even when publishing in journals that mandate it.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 有些人担心分享的潜在影响太大，尤其是在职业生涯的早期阶段。“每个人都有一个关于某人被抢先的可怕故事，”纽约大学天文学家大卫·霍格说。这些担忧可能是人们对共享数据犹豫不决的一个因素，即使在强制要求的期刊上发表数据也是如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. Researchers at small labs or at institutions focused on teaching arguably have the most to lose when sharing hard-won data. ""With my institution and teaching load, I don't have postdocs and grad students", says Terry McGlynn, a tropical biologist at California State University, Dominguez Hills. “The stakes are higher to share data because it's a bigger fraction of what’s happening in my lab.”
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 在共享来之不易的数据时，小型实验室或专注于教学的机构的研究人员可以说损失最大。 “就我的机构和教学负担而言，我没有博士后和研究生”，加州州立大学多明格斯山分校的热带生物学家 Terry McGlynn 说道，“共享数据的风险更大，因为它在我实验室发生的事情中占了更大的比例。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Researchers also point to the time sink that is involved in preparing data for others to view. Once the data and associated materials appear in a repository(存储库), answering questions and handling complaints can take many hours.
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 研究人员还指出了准备数据供其他人查看所涉及的时间消耗。一旦数据和相关材料出现在存储库中，回答问题和处理投诉可能需要几个小时。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. The time investment can present other problems. In some cases, says data scientist Karthik Ram, it may be difficult for junior researchers to embrace openness when senior colleagues— many of whom head selection and promotion committees —might ridicule what they may view as misplaced energies. "I've heard this recently -that embracing the idea of open data and code makes traditional academics uncomfortable, "says Ram. "The concern seems to be that open advocates don't spend their time being as productive as possible."
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 时间投入可能会带来其他问题。数据科学家卡蒂克·拉姆 (Karthik Ram) 表示，在某些情况下，当高级同事（其中许多人担任选拔和晋升委员会负责人）可能会嘲笑他们认为是错误的精力时，初级研究人员可能很难接受开放性。 “我最近听说，接受开放数据和代码的想法让传统学者感到不舒服，”拉姆说。 “令人担心的是，开放倡导者并没有把时间花在尽可能高效的事情上。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K. An open-science stance can also add complexity to a collaboration. Kate Ratliff, who studies social attitudes at the University of Florida, Gainesville, says that it can seem as if there are two camps in a field-those who care about open science and those who don't . " There’s a new area to navigate-‘Are you cool with the fact that I'll want to make the data open?'-when talking with somebody about an interesting research idea, "she says.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 开放科学立场也会增加合作的复杂性。盖恩斯维尔佛罗里达大学研究社会态度的凯特·拉特利夫 (Kate Ratliff) 表示，一个领域似乎存在两个阵营——关心开放科学的人和不关心开放科学的人。 “当与某人谈论一个有趣的研究想法时，有一个新的领域需要导航——‘你对我想要公开数据的事实感到满意吗？’”她说。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. Despite complications and concerns, the upsides of sharing can be significant. For example, when information is uploaded to a repository, a digital object identifier(DOI)is assigned. Scientists can use a DOI to publish each step of the research life cycle, not just the final paper. In so doing, they can potentially get three citations- one each for the data and software. in addition to the paper itself. And although some say that citations for software or data have little currency in academia, they can have other benefits.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 尽管存在复杂性和担忧，但分享的好处仍然是巨大的。例如，当信息上传到存储库时，会分配一个数字对象标识符 (DOI)。科学家可以使用 DOI 来发布研究生命周期的每个步骤，而不仅仅是最终论文。这样一来，他们就有可能获得三次引用——数据和软件各引用一次。除了纸张本身。尽管有人说软件或数据的引用在学术界很少流行，但它们还有其他好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. Many advocates think that transparent data procedures with a date and time stamp will protect scientists from being scooped. "This is the sweet spot between sharing and getting credit for it. while discouraging plagiarism(剽窃). " says Ivo Grigorov, a project coordinator at the National Institute of Aquatic Resources Research Secretariat in Charlottenlund, Denmark. Hogg says that scooping is less of a problem than many think. "The two cases I'm familiar with didn't involve open data or code, "he says.
paragraphs.translationZh: M. 许多倡导者认为，带有日期和时间戳的透明数据程序将保护科学家不被窃取。丹麦夏洛滕隆国家水生资源研究秘书处项目协调员伊沃·格里戈罗夫 (Ivo Grigorov) 表示：“这是分享和获得认可之间的最佳平衡点，同时阻止剽窃。”霍格表示，铲球问题并不像许多人想象的那么严重。 “我熟悉的两个案例并不涉及开放数据或代码，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. Open science also offers junior researchers the chance to level the playing field by gaining better access to crucial date. Ross Mounce, a postdoc studying evolutionary biology at the University of Cambridge, UK, is a vocal champion of open science, partly because his fossil based research on access to others' data. He says that more openness in science could help to discourage what some perceive as a common practice of shutting out early-career scientists' requests for data.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 开放科学还为初级研究人员提供了通过更好地获取关键数据来创造公平竞争环境的机会。英国剑桥大学研究进化生物学的博士后罗斯·穆斯 (Ross Mounce) 是开放科学的坚定拥护者，部分原因是他基于化石的研究是为了获取他人的数据。他说，科学领域更加开放可能有助于阻止某些人认为拒绝早期职业科学家索取数据的普遍做法。

paragraphs.sourceText: O. Communication also helps for those who worry about jeopardizing a collaboration, he says, Concerns about open science should be discussed at the outset of a study. “Whenever you start a project with someone, you have to establish a clear understanding of expectations for who owns the data, at what point they go public and who can do what with them,” he says. [P] In the end, sharing data, software and materials with colleagues can help an early -career researcher to gain recognition--a crucial component of success. "The thing you are searching for reputation" says Titus Brown, a genomics(基因组学) researcher at the University of California, Davis. "To get grants and jobs you have to be relevant and achieve some level of public recognition. Anything you do that advances your presence- especially in a larger sphere, outside the communities you know- is a net win."
paragraphs.translationZh: O. 沟通也有助于那些担心危及合作的人，他说，对开放科学的担忧应该在研究开始时讨论。 “每当你与某人一起启动一个项目时，你都必须清楚地了解对谁拥有这些数据、这些数据何时公开以及谁可以用这些数据做什么的期望，”他说。 [P] 最后，与同事共享数据、软件和材料可以帮助早期职业研究人员获得认可——这是成功的关键组成部分。 “你正在寻找的就是声誉”，加州大学戴维斯分校的基因组学研究员泰特斯·布朗 (Titus Brown) 说。 “为了获得资助和工作，你必须具有相关性并获得一定程度的公众认可。你所做的任何能够提升你的存在感的事情——尤其是在更大的领域，在你所认识的社区之外——都是一个净赢。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Astronomer David Hogg doesn't think scooping is as serious a problem as generally thought.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 天文学家大卫·霍格（David Hogg）认为舀水问题并不像人们普遍认为的那么严重。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Some researchers are hesitant to make their data public for fear that others might publish something similar before them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 一些研究人员不愿公开他们的数据，因为担心其他人可能会在他们之前发表类似的数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Some psychology journals have offered incentives to encourage authors to share their data.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 一些心理学期刊提供奖励措施，鼓励作者分享他们的数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. There is a growing demand in the science community that research data be open to the public.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 科学界越来越要求向公众开放研究数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Sharing data offers early-career researchers the chance to build a certain level of reputation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 共享数据为处于职业生涯早期的研究人员提供了建立一定声誉的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Data sharing enables scientists to publish each step of their research work, thus leading to more citations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 数据共享使科学家能够发表其研究工作的每一步，从而导致更多的引用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Scientists hold different opinions about the extent and timing of data sharing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 科学家对数据共享的程度和时间持有不同意见。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Potential problems related to data sharing should be made known to and discussed by all participants at the beginning of a joint research project.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 与数据共享相关的潜在问题应在联合研究项目开始时告知所有参与者并由所有参与者进行讨论。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Sharing data and handling data-related issues can be time-consuming.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 共享数据和处理数据相关问题可能非常耗时。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Junior researchers may have no say when it comes to sharing data.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 初级研究人员在共享数据方面可能没有发言权。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the beginning of the movie l, Robot, a robot has to decide whom to save after two cars plunge into the water-Del Spooner or a child. Even though Spooner screams “Save her Save her!” the robot rescues him because it calculates that he has a 45 percent chance of survival compared to Sarah's 11 percent. The robot's decision and its calculated approach raise an important question: would humans make the same choice? And which choice would we want our robotic counterparts to make?
paragraphs.translationZh: 在电影《机器人》的开头，两辆汽车落入水中后，机器人必须决定救谁——德尔·斯普纳还是孩子。尽管斯普纳尖叫着“救救她救救她！”机器人救了他，因为它计算出他有 45% 的生存机会，而莎拉的生存机会只有 11%。机器人的决定及其计算方法提出了一个重要问题：人类会做出同样的选择吗？我们希望我们的机器人同行做出哪种选择？

paragraphs.sourceText: Isaac Asimov evaded the whole notion of morality in devising his three laws of robotics, which hold that 1. Robots cannot harm humans or allow humans to come to harm; 2. Robots must obey humans, except where the order would conflict with law 1; and 3. Robots must act in self-preservation, unless doing so conflicts with laws 1 or 2. These laws are programmed into Asimov's robots-they don' t have to think, judge, or value. They don't have to like humans or believe that hurting them is wrong or bad. They simply don't do it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 艾萨克·阿西莫夫（Isaac Asimov）在设计他的机器人三定律时回避了整个道德概念，该定律认为： 1. 机器人不能伤害人类或允许人类受到伤害； 2. 机器人必须服从人类，除非该命令与法律1相冲突； 3. 机器人的行为必须出于自我保护，除非这样做与定律 1 或 2 相冲突。这些定律被编程到阿西莫夫的机器人中——它们不需要思考、判断或价值。他们不必喜欢人类或认为伤害人类是错误或不好的。他们就是不这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: The robot who rescues Spooner’s life in I, Robot follows Asimov's zeroth law: robots cannot harm humanity(as opposed to individual humans)or allow humanity to come to harm--an expansion of the first law that allows robots to determine what's in the greater good. Under the first law, a robot could not harm a dangerous gunman, but under the zeroth law, a robot could kill the gunman to save others.
paragraphs.translationZh: 《我，机器人》中拯救斯普纳生命的机器人遵循阿西莫夫的第零定律：机器人不能伤害人类（相对于人类个体）或允许人类受到伤害——这是第一定律的扩展，该定律允许机器人决定什么是更大的利益。根据第一定律，机器人不能伤害危险的枪手，但根据第零定律，机器人可以杀死枪手以拯救他人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Whether it's possible to program a robot with safeguards such as Asimov's laws is debatable A word such as "harm" is vague (what about emotional harm? Is replacing a human employ harm?), and abstract concepts present coding problems. The robots in Asimov's fiction expose complications and loopholes in the three laws, and even when the laws work, robots still have to assess situations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 是否有可能为机器人编写具有阿西莫夫定律等保障措施的程序是值得商榷的。像“伤害”这样的词是模糊的（情感伤害呢？取代人类雇佣伤害吗？），抽象概念带来了编码问题。阿西莫夫小说中的机器人暴露了三大定律的复杂性和漏洞，即使这些定律起作用，机器人仍然必须评估情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: Assessing situations can be complicated. A robot has to identify the players, conditions, and possible outcomes for various scenarios, It’s doubtful that a computer program can do that-at least, not without some undesirable results. A roboticist at the Bristol Robotics Laboratory programmed a robot to save human proxies(替身) called "H-bots" from danger.
paragraphs.translationZh: 评估情况可能很复杂。机器人必须识别不同场景的玩家、条件和可能的结果，计算机程序能否做到这一点值得怀疑——至少，不会出现一些不良结果。布里斯托尔机器人实验室的一名机器人专家编写了一个机器人来拯救被称为“H-bots”的人类代理（替身）免受危险。

paragraphs.sourceText: When one H-bot headed for danger, the robot successfully pushed it out of the way. But when two H-bots became imperiled, the robot choked 42 percent of the time, unable to decide which to save and letting them both "die. "The experiment highlights the importance of morality: without it, how can a robot decide whom to save or what's best for humanity, especially if it can't calculate survival odds?
paragraphs.translationZh: 当一台 H 机器人走向危险时，机器人成功地将其推开。但当两台 H 机器人陷入危险时，机器人有 42% 的概率会被噎住，无法决定拯救哪一个，从而让它们都“死去”。该实验凸显了道德的重要性：如果没有道德，机器人如何决定拯救谁或什么对人类最好，尤其是在它无法计算生存几率的情况下？

paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 5i 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Our world now moves so fast that we seldom stop to see just how far we have come in just a few years. The latest iPhone 6s,for example, has a dual-core processor and fits nicely into your pocket. By comparison, you would expect to find a technological specification like this on your standard laptop in an office anywhere in the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们的世界现在发展得如此之快，以至于我们很少停下来看看我们在短短几年内已经走了多远。例如，最新的 iPhone 6s 配备双核处理器，非常适合放入口袋中。相比之下，您可能希望在世界任何地方的办公室的标准笔记本电脑上找到这样的技术规格。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s no wonder shat new applications for the Internet of Things are moving ahead fast when almost every new device we buy has a plug on the end of it or a wireless connection to the internet. Soon, our current smartphone lifestyle will expand to create our own smart home lifestyle too.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当我们购买的几乎每台新设备末端都有插头或无线连接到互联网时，物联网的新应用程序正在快速发展也就不足为奇了。很快，我们当前的智能手机生活方式也将扩展到创建我们自己的智能家居生活方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: All researches agree that close to 25 billion devices, things and sensors will be connected by 2020 which incidentally is also the moment that Millennials(千禧一代) are expected to make up 75 percent of our overall workforce, and the fully connected home . become a reality for large numbers of people worldwide.
paragraphs.translationZh: 所有研究都一致认为，到 2020 年，将有近 250 亿台设备、物体和传感器连接起来，顺便说一句，千禧一代预计将占我们劳动力总数的 75％，并且家庭将完全联网。成为全世界许多人的现实。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, this is just the tip of the proverbial iceberg as smart buildings and even cities increasingly become the norm as leaders and business owners begin to wake up to the massive savings that technology can deliver through connected sensors and new forms of automation coupled with intelligent energy and facilities management.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，这只是众所周知的冰山一角，随着智能建筑甚至城市日益成为常态，领导者和企业主开始意识到技术可以通过连接传感器和新型自动化以及智能能源和设施管理来节省大量成本。

paragraphs.sourceText: Online security cameras, intelligent lighting and a wealth of sensors that control both temperature and air quality are offering an unprecedented level of control, efficiency, and improvements to what were once classed necessary costs when running a business or managing a large building.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在线安全摄像头、智能照明和大量控制温度和空气质量的传感器正在提供前所未有的控制水平、效率，并改善了经营企业或管理大型建筑时曾经被视为必要的成本。

paragraphs.sourceText: We can expect that the ever-growing list of devices, systems and environments remain connected, always online and talking to each other. The big benefit will not only be in the housing of this enormous and rapidly growing amount of data, but will also be in the ability to run real time data analytics to extract actionable and ongoing knowledge.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们可以预期，不断增长的设备、系统和环境仍然保持连接、始终在线并相互通信。巨大的好处不仅在于存储如此巨大且快速增长的数据量，还在于能够运行实时数据分析以提取可操作的持续知识。

paragraphs.sourceText: The biggest and most exciting challenge of this technology is how to creatively leverage this ever-growing amount of data to deliver cost savings, improvements and tangible benefits to both businesses and citizens of these smart cities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这项技术最大、最令人兴奋的挑战是如何创造性地利用这些不断增长的数据量，为这些智慧城市的企业和公民带来成本节约、改进和切实的好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: The good news is that most of this technology is already invented. Let's face it, it wasn't too long ago that the idea of working from anywhere and at anytime was some form of a distant utopian(乌托邦式的) dream, and yet now we can perform almost any office-based task from any location in the world as long as we have access to the internet.
paragraphs.translationZh: 好消息是大部分这项技术已经被发明出来。让我们面对现实吧，不久前，随时随地工作的想法还只是某种遥远的乌托邦式的梦想，但现在，只要我们能够访问互联网，我们就可以在世界任何地点执行几乎任何基于办公室的任务。

paragraphs.sourceText: It's time to wake up to the fact that making smart buildings, cities and homes will dramatically improve our quality of life in the years ahead.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在是时候认识到这样一个事实了：建造智能建筑、城市和家庭将在未来几年极大地改善我们的生活质量。
